item.title: UK approves drilling at controversial North Sea gas field despite environmental concerns
item.description: The Shell Group, one of the project's co-developers, predicts the field can produce around 6.5% of the UK’s gas production at its peak.

item.title: What does Lufthansa gain from its €1.2 billion TAP Air Portugal deal and when?
item.description: Lufthansa expects about €450 million a year in synergies from buying up to 49.9% of TAP Air Portugal for €1.2 billion, but Portugal’s continued control, lengthy regulatory reviews and the slow progress of its ITA Airways deal suggest the gains could take years to arrive.

item.title: Large crowds watch as rescuers try to save stranded shark in South Korea
item.description: Officials in Busan made a third attempt to guide a trapped shark out of a canal and back to sea. The animal has drawn over a million visitors.

item.title: Trump tells companies to pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
item.description: The US President made the comments on his social media platform Truth Social on Wednesday, encouraging companies to strike deals with local communities to make data centre developments more popular.

item.title: Trump is taking Russia's side against Ukraine, former US general tells Euronews
item.description: Former US Army lieutenant General Ben Hodges warns that Washington’s approach is weakening Ukraine’s defences, while former US ambassador to NATO Kurt Volker urges Europe to prepare for a future with less American support.

item.title: No kids invited: A new travel package offers a child-free flight and adults-only cruise
item.description: JetBlue Vacations has teamed up with Virgin Voyages for a four-night trip on board Brilliant Lady which includes a dedicated adults-only flight from New York.

item.title: Restorers work to preserve frescoes in one of Pompeii’s grandest Roman houses
item.description: Nearly 2,000 years after Mount Vesuvius buried Pompeii in volcanic ash, one of the ancient Roman city's grandest homes is getting a new lease of life.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 21st, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 21st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: French government 10-year bond yield tops 5% for first time since 2002
item.description: The yield on the French government's benchmark 10-year bond surpassed 5% on Wednesday as investors demanded a higher return for holding the country's debt.

item.title: Former Hungarian central bank chief György Matolcsy detained in financial fraud probe
item.description: The investigation follows scrutiny of the central bank's foundations, which managed more than €1 billion in public funds. Matolcsy has denied wrongdoing.

item.title: More Russians are settling in the EU with each year of war in Ukraine
item.description: Eurostat data show 876,600 Russian nationals held valid EU residence permits at the end of 2025, with Germany, Spain and Estonia hosting the largest communities.

item.title: Hansel and Gretel in the mountains: parents abandon sons in Germany
item.description: In South Tyrol, parents on a hike let their sons climb alone to a mountain hut. They turn back, but the hut is closed and the children are left to fend for themselves at 2,300 metres.

item.title: UK inflation jumps more than expected fuelling rate hike expectations
item.description: Britain's annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5% on surging fuel prices. This comes a week before the UK government presents its autumn budget and as UK public sector net debt tops £3 trillion.

item.title: ‘A house cannot be a privilege’: Thousands rally in Lisbon over housing crisis
item.description: Thousands protested in Lisbon’s Rossio square over housing costs after police removed a camp, and voted to return the next day to camp out again.

item.title: A stunning Alpine retreat will open at the foot of the Dolomites this winter
item.description: Le Graal Cortina will have just 30 rooms, including 13 suites, when it opens in Cortina d'Ampezzo.

item.title: Italy deploys 500 troops to Milan under new security decree following violent clashes
item.description: Meloni said nearly 200 police officers had been injured and 330 people detained, around half of whom she said were of "foreign origin".

item.title: New Beatles attraction ‘to rival Graceland' coming to Liverpool in 2028
item.description: The new 9,290-square-metre site in the heart of Liverpool has been compared to Graceland and Dollywood and will repurpose the iconic St Johns Beacon into a viewing tower.

item.title: High rent and expensive food: Can the EU help citizens deal with inflation?
item.description: Volatile energy prices have pushed consumer price indices across major EU economies. Now, they nearly double the ECB’s inflation target of 2%.

item.title: Attacked owner of looted Paris shop: '10 years of work destroyed, I have not slept in three days'
item.description: Originally from Bangladesh, Hassan arrived in France in 2010. After spending years working in hospitality, he managed to save enough to open his own business. In the aftermath of the weekend riots in Paris, his shop has been left completely destroyed.

item.title: Cleanup efforts begin in flood-hit eastern Spain after deadly torrential rain
item.description: Torrential rain flooded eastern Spain, leaving at least four dead. Crews carried out more than 400 rescues in the Valencia region, officials said Monday.

item.title: 'Failures of the past have consequences today' says Fabrice Leggeri on recent French protests
item.description: Fabrice Leggeri, MEP for Rassemblement Nationale speaks to Euronews on the recent violence and protests in France.

item.title: Dramatic footage shows ferry engulfed in flames off Indonesia
item.description: All passengers and crew were rescued after the KMP Batumandi ferry caught fire near Merak Port in western Indonesia on Tuesday.

item.title: Arctic gas and oil should 'stay in the ground', says EU commissioner Síkela
item.description: European Commissioner for International Partnerships Jozef Síkela insists the EU will maintain its opposition to drilling for natural resources, including oil and gas, in the Arctic, despite the US and Norway taking a different approach.

item.title: More cuts 'necessary' says German ambassador to EU, ruling out common borrowing, EU-level taxes
item.description: More cuts are "definitely necessary", says German ambassador to the EU. Thomas Hans Ossowki speaks on EU budget discussions, ruling out new common borrowing and EU-level taxation, while reaffirming support for Ukraine.

item.title: Diplomatic damage control in Oslo as Zelenskyy says US intelligence sharing restored
item.description: Good morning. It’s Mared Gwyn, penning this newsletter in the early hours from Brussels. In this edition: The diplomatic push to revive Ukraine peace talks, and how Hungary has surprised diplomats by stalling Kyiv’s accession talks.

item.title: AI and digital transformation reshape aviation, but safety remains non-negotiable
item.description: At the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Hitit CEO Nevra Onursal Karaağaç and digital transformation lead Aras Kubilay urged gradual modernisation of airline systems and warned of the risks of adopting AI without a clear strategy.

item.title: US envoy in Russia for Putin talks after 'positive' Zelenskyy meeting
item.description: Moscow says it is prepared to consider economic proposals from Washington but will not make political concessions, while the Kremlin insists that a lasting settlement on Russia's terms, rather than a temporary energy ceasefire, remains its objective.

item.title: Europe’s pensions rank among the world’s best – but how secure are they?
item.description: A new ranking of 55 retirement income systems reveals how Europe’s pension systems compare, with concerns over the long-term sustainability of benefits in some of the continent’s largest economies.

item.title: How toxic wildfire haze is affecting daily life in Indonesia's cities
item.description: Wildfires have blanketed Palangkaraya, on the Indonesian island of Borneo, in toxic haze for weeks, leaving residents struggling with persistent coughs, falling incomes and disrupted education.

item.title: Europe Today: France to deploy army before weekend protests as Italy tightens powers
item.description: France will put soldiers on the streets ahead of more weekend protests, after days of violence and vandalism. Italy is giving police new powers, Albania's protests enter a second week, and Greek students march today. In Oslo, Steve Witkoff meets Zelenskyy before heading to Moscow.

item.title: 'This is possible': Emissions must fall by 18% in next 4 years to limit worst impacts of global warming
item.description: “Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5°C increases climate impacts and risks, such as the deadly floods, heatwaves and wildfires that have plagued many nations this year”.

item.title: Netflix shares drop on slowing engagement and revenue growth
item.description: Netflix shares fell after its latest earnings failed to cheer investors as the streaming giant faces mounting competition and reportedly plans to cut around 1,000 jobs.

item.title: Greece tourism: August 2026 arrivals up 2.6%, with foreign visitors leading growth
item.description: Arrivals reached 7.43 million and overnight stays 34.69 million, with short-stay rentals up 5.2%, compared with just 1.5% for hotels and campsites.

item.title: What is Spain’s DANA weather phenomenon and is climate change making it worse?
item.description: A DANA caused the deadly flooding in Valencia in 2024 which killed 200 people.

item.title: Trump’s embrace of Putin roils Europe, but not enough to break with the US
item.description: Donald Trump's embrace of Vladimir Putin has driven a wedge between the transatlantic allies. But for all their outrage, Europeans are not yet ready to break away from the United States and go their own way.

item.title: A chilled stay: Europe’s coolest ice, snow and igloo hotels to visit this winter
item.description: If you’re planning a winter escape, why not embrace the cold and check into an ice, snow or igloo hotel? From seasonal ‘properties’ in Swedish and Finnish Lapland to a year-round icy stay in Norway, here are five places in Europe for a cool getaway.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 21st, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 21st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: From ‘sleepmaxxing’ to rising temperatures: getting a good night's sleep is getting harder
item.description: Climate change, unequal access to healthcare and an ‘always-on’ work culture are undermining sleep across Europe — essential for good health.

item.title: Elon Musk backs SpaceX-Tesla merger as rocket firm turns profit
item.description: Elon Musk has signalled his support for a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla, as SpaceX reported a sharp rise in revenue and its first quarterly profit since going public.

item.title: Alberta’s “no” to separation gives Carney a boost as Trump pressure unites Canadians
item.description: Roughly three in four voters rejected starting a path toward separation, as Trump’s trade war and annexation threats push Canadians closer together.

item.title: New Romanian prime minister Luca Niculescu and cabinet members sworn in
item.description: Independent diplomat Luca Niculescu wins parliamentary backing for a minority government, but analysts warn the calm may not last.

item.title: Dutch Crown Princess Amalia promoted to sergeant in naval ceremony
item.description: Dutch Crown Princess Amalia was promoted to sergeant aboard a Norwegian training ship in Den Helder, where she has been sailing alongside first-year naval cadets.

item.title: Severe weather in southern France: one dead near Marseille, one missing in Corsica
item.description: In Haute-Corse, a person went missing in Ghisonaccia on Tuesday evening; another was found dead in Saint-Mitre-les-Remparts in the Bouches-du-Rhône.

item.title: 'Time to make a deal,' Trump tells Zelenskyy as he complains US has got 'nothing back' from Ukraine
item.description: Trump's comments came shortly after Zelenskyy met with a US delegation headed by special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.

item.title: Spain: Guardia Civil rescues family and dogs from rising floodwaters in Oliva
item.description: Spanish Guardia Civil officers have rescued a family and their dogs from a flooded home in Oliva, in eastern Spain. Dramatic footage shows officers carrying residents to safety as floodwaters engulf the town, while aerial images reveal the extent of the flooding across the Valencia region.

item.title: UK Typhoon fighter jets to fly 'defensive' missions to help protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
item.description: British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting branded Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as "absolutely despicable and dangerous for the region."

item.title: Investment summit: German government strikes AI deal with Nvidia
item.description: At the "Invest in Germany" summit in Berlin, the federal government, despite early negative headlines, secured a partnership with AI firm Nvidia and new investment from Amazon.

item.title: EU Parliament approves standard form for claiming refunds on disrupted travel
item.description: Passengers across Europe are entitled to a full refund within 14 days, even if they booked through a travel intermediary. Companions of people with disabilities will fly free of charge.

item.title: France's Macron begins state visit to Qatar as part of wider Gulf tour
item.description: Qatar welcomed the French president with full state honours on his arrival in Doha as the two countries are strengthening their strategic ties. Facing protests at home, Macron is seeking energy deals with Gulf partners to help ease fuel prices in France, but also contributing to regional stability.

item.title: IRGC mines set tankers ablaze as Tehran threatens expanded attacks
item.description: Iran’s foreign ministry further warned Washington it would retaliate against any strike, and an IRGC spokesperson threatened to target undersea internet cables in the Gulf in another escalation of the ongoing war of words between Tehran and Washington.
